current.text: He is coming back from a torn Achilles, more than 12 months after the injury. The GM expects him ready for opening night. He says he has no restrictions.

Experts expect a slow start: rust, a ramp-up period, some missed games and short minutes limits early. Coach Rick Carlisle is expected to manage his minutes, and McConnell and Nembhard can handle the role.
Tony expects about 30 minutes in games without a back-to-back. Back-to-backs may be monitored or limited to one game.
Some experts worry about compensation injuries after the Achilles tear.
Experts expect rust on his percentages and a small dip in usage and efficiency early. One worry is that his two-point percentage drops from about 59 to 57.

He should be close to his best later in the season: after Christmas or by January, and fine by the fantasy playoffs. The speaker does not expect 34 minutes per game over the full season, but that might come by the fantasy playoffs.
He has the widest range of outcomes among round-one ADP players. Best case 8th, worst case 55th.

In category leagues, experts rank him in the 14 to 20 range. They call the Yahoo rank of 10 too aggressive and picks 10 to 13 a little early. The middle of round 2 is fine and the end of round 1 is acceptable.
In an auction, Josh would not pay more than 35 USD. In a mock auction he went for 36 USD, which Josh called a little high.
Indiana projects him as a starter next to Nembhard, Nesmith, Siakam and Zubac.
Experts expect Indiana to be good. They project 46 to 48 wins and a top-six seed in the East.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, which is not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He tore his Achilles in the June 2025 NBA Finals and missed the whole next season. He also had a case of shingles.
He is an elite assist source and always a threat to lead the league in assists. Draft him early if you want assists.
He is not a high scorer or a high usage player. Taking him in round one pushes a team toward punting points.
He is a great shooter. He made just under 40% of his threes in his last full season.
His steals and FG% have been good, and two-point finishing is a strength.
He is very good at picking apart confused defenses, and he does it with very few turnovers.
How he plays shapes the fantasy value of every other Pacer.
Coach Rick Carlisle keeps players' minutes low even when they are healthy, and he rests players on back-to-backs.
Experts say he is not a top player in Yahoo points leagues even when healthy, because that scoring does not suit his game. They rate him higher in category leagues.

note: Yahoo values him at 49 USD with a 45.4 USD average cost, and ESPN's average cost is 39.1 USD. The newest expert cap is 35 USD, and experts rank him 14 to 20 rather than 10th, so let him go at Yahoo prices and buy in the high 30s at most. He fits any build as an elite assist source with useful threes and steals. Early in the season, check his minutes, how he handles back-to-backs and his two-point efficiency. Our playoff weeks give him only 10 games (3-4-3).
